label: Open to anyone
help: On: anyone can join, and their account is made the first time they log in with a password. Off: only people already on the whitelist (or allowed Steam IDs) can join. The Indie Stone's Build 42 multiplayer notes suggest a whitelisted server, so off.

label: Welcome message
help: The message shown in chat right after a player logs in. Use <LINE> for a new line and <RGB:1,0,0> for colour.

label: Refuse logins when overloaded
help: On: while the server is dropping network packets, new logins are refused with 'Server is too busy.' The game only checks this on a server hosted from inside the game with Steam on, so it has no effect on a dedicated server.

label: Maximum players
help: How many players can be on at once. When it's full, new joiners are refused with 'ServerFull', or wait in the queue if 'Login queue' is on. The Indie Stone's Build 42 notes suggest 20 players or fewer.

label: Ping limit (ms)
help: Players whose ping stays above this, in milliseconds, are kicked, and players above it when they join are turned away. 0 turns this off. While playing, each ping over 1000 counts as 1000, so a value of 1000 or more never kicks anyone already in. Staff with the right permission are never kicked for lag.

label: Remove from whitelist on death
help: On: when a character dies, the player's account is taken off the whitelist. On a closed server ('Open to anyone' off) they can't come back without an admin.

label: Server password
help: A password everyone must type to join. Leave empty for no password. A /reloadoptions applies a new password without a restart.

label: Accounts per Steam user
help: How many different accounts one Steam user can create here. 0 means no limit. Only checked when the server runs in Steam mode.

label: Split-screen players allowed
help: On: a player can bring extra split-screen players on the same PC. Off: only the first player on each PC can join.

label: Login queue
help: On: players joining a busy or full server wait in a queue instead of being refused. Staff with priority login skip ahead.

label: Queue connect time (seconds)
help: Seconds a queued player gets to finish connecting when it's their turn, before the next person is let in.

label: Non-English letters in usernames
help: On: usernames can use letters outside basic English, for example Cyrillic. Checked when an account logs in.

label: Listed publicly
help: On: the server is listed in the in-game public server browser.

label: Server name
help: The server name shown in the in-game browser and the Steam browser. The game sets 64 characters as the limit for this but doesn't enforce it when the server starts, so keep it to 64 or fewer.

label: Server description
help: The description shown in the in-game public server browser. The game sets 256 characters as the limit for this but doesn't enforce it when the server starts, so keep it to 256 or fewer.

label: Steam names in player list
help: On: the player list shows Steam names and avatars.

label: Steam VAC anti-cheat
help: On: Steam's VAC anti-cheat is switched on for this server. A -steamvac value on the command line overrides this.

label: Open router ports (UPnP)
help: On: the server asks your router to open its ports automatically when it starts. If the server hangs while starting, switch this off.

label: Announced IP address
help: Forces the IP address the server sends to the in-game public server list. Left empty, the server uses the address the list site reports back to it. The game asks for an IPv4 address here when that reported address looks like IPv6.

label: Account names above heads
help: On: account names show above players' heads.

label: Character names above heads
help: On: the character's first and last name show above their head.

label: Face coverings disguise names
help: On: a player whose face is covered shows a 'disguised' name instead of their own.

label: Hide disguised names fully
help: On: disguised players show no name at all instead of the 'disguised' label. This switches disguises on by itself, even with 'Face coverings disguise names' off.

label: Fixed spawn point
help: Forces every new character to start at these x,y,z map coordinates. 0,0,0 means use the normal spawn choices.

label: Starting items
help: Items every new character starts with, as item types separated by commas, for example Base.Axe,Base.Bag_BigHikingBag.

label: No fire (except campfires)
help: On: fire is disabled in multiplayer, except campfires.

label: Sledgehammer destruction
help: On: players can smash world objects and walls with a sledgehammer.

label: Sledgehammer only in own safehouse
help: On: players who aren't admins can only sledgehammer things inside their own safehouse. Needs 'Sledgehammer destruction' on.

label: Sleeping allowed
help: On: players can sleep in beds and cars, and when everyone online is asleep, time speeds up. Usually off on public servers.

label: Sleep needed
help: On: characters get tired and must sleep. Only works when 'Sleeping allowed' is also on.

label: Players can be knocked down
help: On: players can be knocked down. The game marks this as work in progress that may cause position desync.

label: Sneaking hides players
help: On: sneaking players can stay hidden from other players. Each watcher's game rolls a chance to spot them based on distance, light, cover and their Sneaking level, but anyone within 2 tiles, or sprinting, is always seen. Off: sneaking doesn't hide anyone.

label: Animals ignore fast time
help: On: while time runs very fast, for example while everyone sleeps, the game adjusts how quickly animals get hungry and thirsty and makes them wander less often.

label: Respawn where you died
help: On: a player who dies can respawn at the spot where they died.

label: Respawn next to a partner
help: On: a player who dies can respawn next to a split-screen partner on the same PC.

label: Sleep fast forward speed
help: How fast time runs while everyone online is asleep, which needs 'Sleeping allowed'. It's measured against a 30 minute day whatever 'Day length' is set to, so 40 passes a day in about 45 real seconds, and zombies break doors and barricades faster by the same amount.

label: Item limit per container
help: The most items one container can hold, counting every small item such as each nail and everything inside bags. 0 means no limit. What players carry isn't limited, and an empty container takes anything, even a full bag.

label: Remove player bodies too
help: On: dead players' bodies are also removed when the corpse removal timer in the sandbox settings clears bodies.

label: Delete all button on bins
help: On: players get a 'delete all' button on bins.

label: Names only on mouse over
help: On: you only see another player's name when you point your mouse at them.

label: Hide players behind you
help: On: other players behind your character are hidden, the same way zombies you can't see are hidden.

label: Players bump into each other
help: On: players running into each other bump, and the one running can trip and fall. Sprinting into someone always ends in a fall.

label: Players shown on the map
help: Which other players appear on the in-game map: 1 nobody, 2 faction and safehouse mates, 3 those plus players you can see, 4 everyone. Staff who can see the world map always see everyone.

label: Show map coordinates
help: On: players see their map coordinates in the lower right corner.

label: Players can claim safehouses
help: On: any player can claim one building as a safehouse once they've survived the days you set, even if 'Admins only safehouses' is also on. If both are off, nobody can claim a safehouse.

label: Admins only safehouses
help: On, with 'Players can claim safehouses' off: only admins and moderators get the option to claim safehouses, and they can hold more than one. If 'Players can claim safehouses' is also on, this makes no difference and anyone can claim.

label: Non-members can enter safehouses
help: On: people who aren't members can walk into a safehouse. Off: only members can. The game spells this setting Trepass.

label: Fire damages safehouses
help: On: fire can damage safehouses.

label: Non-members can loot safehouses
help: On: people who aren't members can take items from a safehouse.

label: Respawn in your safehouse
help: On: a player who dies can respawn inside a safehouse they belong to, once they've ticked the respawn box in that safehouse's window.

label: Days survived to claim a safehouse
help: In-game days a character must survive before they can claim a safehouse. 0 means straight away.

label: Unvisited safehouse removal (hours)
help: Real-world hours a safehouse can go unvisited before it's removed. 0 turns removal off.

label: Claim non-home buildings
help: On: players can also claim shops and other buildings that aren't homes.

label: No disguises in safehouses
help: On: name disguises don't work inside safehouses.

label: Largest safezone size
help: The largest area a safezone claim can cover, as width times height in tiles. 0 means no limit.

label: Safehouse wars
help: On: safehouse wars can happen, and during a war safehouse protection is lifted.

label: War warning time (seconds)
help: Seconds of warning before a war begins.

label: War length (seconds)
help: How long a war lasts, in seconds.

label: War refusals before loss
help: Only matters when 'Safehouse wars' is on. Each war declared on a safehouse that the owner refuses or doesn't answer in time counts once, and when the count reaches this number the safehouse is released. Wars that are accepted and fought don't count, and 0 means it's never released this way.

label: Protection only while owner is offline
help: On: a safehouse acts like a normal house while its owner or any member is online, so its protection only applies while they're all offline.

label: Factions allowed
help: On: players can create factions.

label: Days survived to make a faction
help: In-game days a character must survive before creating a faction. 0 means straight away.

label: Members needed for a faction tag
help: How many members a faction needs before its owner can set a name tag.

label: PvP
help: On: players can hurt and kill each other. Usually off, or on with 'PvP safety switch' so players can switch their own PvP on and off.

label: PvP reports in admin chat
help: On: PvP events are reported in admin chat.

label: PvP events in log files
help: On: PvP events are written to the server log files.

label: PvP safety switch
help: Only matters when PvP is on. On: each player chooses whether they're open to PvP, and a hit is only blocked when both players have it switched off, so a player who has it on can also hurt players who have it off. Off: everyone can hurt everyone.

label: Skull over PvP players
help: On: a skull shows over players who have PvP switched on.

label: PvP switch-off delay
help: Turning PvP on is instant. Turning it back off keeps the player open to PvP for this many real seconds first, and the switch can't be used again until then. 0 makes it instant.

label: PvP combat cooldown
help: Real seconds added to a player's cooldown each time they attack another player while open to PvP, stacking with each attack. They can't change their PvP switch until it runs out. 0 adds none.

label: PvP logout delay
help: Only matters when 'PvP' and the 'PvP safety switch' are on. If a player leaves while their switch is changing or their attack cooldown is running, their character stays in the world for twice this many seconds, longer if they're hit, and their quit buttons stay greyed out until the cooldown ends. 0 turns this off.

label: Hit back straight away in PvP
help: On: a player who has just been hit by another player can swing back straight away.

label: PvP melee damage
help: Multiplies melee damage when one player hits another. It's a straight multiplier, not a percentage, so 1 leaves damage unchanged and the default 30 is 30 times that.

label: PvP firearm damage
help: Multiplies ranged weapon damage when one player shoots another. It's a straight multiplier, not a percentage, so 1 leaves damage unchanged and the default 50 is 50 times that.

label: Global chat
help: On: the global /all chat channel is available.

label: Chat channels
help: Which chat channels exist, as short codes separated by commas: s say, r radio, a admin, w whisper, y yell, sh safehouse, f faction, all global (only if 'Global chat' is on).

label: Announce player deaths
help: On: a message goes to everyone in chat whenever a player dies.

label: Announce animal deaths
help: On: a message goes to everyone in chat when a player kills an animal.

label: Voice chat
help: On: built-in voice chat is available.

label: Voice full volume range
help: Within this many tiles, other players' voice chat plays at full volume. Further out it fades smoothly to silence at 'Voice hearing range'.

label: Voice hearing range
help: Beyond this many tiles, voice chat is silent, and between 'Voice full volume range' and this it fades smoothly. Voice heard through a radio uses the radio's own range instead.

label: Directional voice
help: On: voice chat sounds come from the speaker's direction.

label: Block radio for all staff
help: On: players with the admin, GM or moderator role can't send chat messages out over in-game radios. Overseers aren't covered.

label: Block radio for admins
help: On: admins can't send chat messages out over in-game radios.

label: Block radio for GMs
help: On: GMs can't send chat messages out over in-game radios.

label: Block radio for overseers
help: Meant to stop overseers sending chat messages over in-game radios, but the game only checks it for admins, GMs and moderators, so this has no effect.

label: Block radio for moderators
help: On: moderators can't send chat messages out over in-game radios.

label: Block radio for invisible staff
help: On: invisible staff can't transmit on in-game radios.

label: Banned words file
help: Path to a text file of banned words, one per line, for the chat filter. The file is read once at start, so edits take effect after a restart.

label: Allowed words file
help: Path to a text file of allowed words, one per line. The chat filter won't block these even if they contain a banned word. The file is read once at start, so edits take effect after a restart.

label: Banned word penalty
help: What happens to someone who uses a banned word: they're banned, kicked, or the violation is just recorded. Their message is still sent, with the word replaced.

label: Banned word replacement
help: The text that replaces a banned word in chat, up to 16 characters.

label: Chat message length limit
help: The longest chat message a player can type, in characters.

label: Chat slow mode (seconds)
help: How many seconds a player must wait between chat messages.

label: Discord bot on
help: On: the server's built-in Discord bot connects and relays chat. Read when the server starts, so changes take effect after a restart.

label: Discord bot token
help: The access token for the Discord bot the server logs in as. Keep this secret; the game leaves it out of the public option list.

label: Discord chat channel
help: The Discord channel name (not the ID) for relaying chat. The bot uses the first text channel with this name.

label: Discord log channel
help: The Discord channel name (not the ID) where the bot posts log messages.

label: Discord command channel
help: The Discord channel name (not the ID) where the bot listens for commands. Anything posted there runs as a server command with admin rights, so only let people you trust post in that channel.

label: Slack webhook address
help: A webhook web address. When this is filled in, server events are posted there as a JSON message with a text field. The game's tooltip calls it a Slack incoming webhook.

label: RCON password
help: The password for the remote console. Leave this empty and RCON stays off. Keep it secret.

label: Mod IDs
help: The mod IDs to load, separated by semicolons. Backslashes are removed before the list is read, so Build 42 IDs work with or without a leading backslash.

label: Map folders
help: The map folders to load, separated by semicolons. Where two maps cover the same area, the one earlier in the list wins.

label: Check players' files match
help: On: players whose game or mod files don't match the server's are refused.

label: Workshop item numbers
help: Steam Workshop item numbers the server downloads at start, separated by semicolons. Each mod also needs its mod ID listed in 'Mod IDs'.

label: Auto save (minutes)
help: Saves the loaded parts of the map every this many real minutes. 0 means only the normal saving, when areas unload.

label: Backups to keep
help: How many backups the server keeps of each kind: at startup, after a game version change, and on the backup timer. Each kind keeps its own set, so you can have up to three times this number, and when a set is full the oldest one is deleted.

label: Back up on start
help: On: a backup is made every time the server starts.

label: Back up when version changes
help: On: a backup is made at start when the game version is different from the last run.

label: Timed backups (minutes)
help: Makes a backup every this many real minutes while the server's running. 0 turns timed backups off.

label: World seed
help: The world generation seed. The game only uses this when the world's generation data doesn't exist yet. Its tooltip says to delete map_worldgen.bin in the save to change it.

label: Pause when empty
help: On: game time stops while nobody's online.

label: Rotate zombie control
help: On: with more than one player online, control of each zombie passes to the next connected player every 2 seconds, in turn. Off: each zombie is run by the player grabbing or chasing it, or else the nearest player.

label: Blood splat lifespan (unused server copy)
help: The game uses the sandbox setting with the same name instead of this one.

label: Car noise range for zombies
help: Multiplies how far a running car's noise reaches zombies, on top of 'Engine loudness to zombies'. Lower values make the noise pulse more often over a smaller area, and it never drops below a radius of 8, so 0 doesn't make cars silent.

label: Multiplayer stats interval (seconds)
help: How often, in seconds, the server gathers multiplayer statistics. 0 turns statistics off.

label: Packet limit per second
help: The most packets of any one kind a player's game sends each second. Past the limit their game skips the extra packets, while the server only notes it in its debug log and doesn't kick anyone.

label: Ragdoll hit reactions
help: The game doesn't use this in 42.21. Ragdolls are switched off on every multiplayer server and client before this is checked.

label: Thunder on ban or kick
help: On: everyone hears thunder when staff ban or kick a player who's online. Automatic bans and kicks by the anti-cheat or the banned word filter don't play it.

label: Anti-cheat: PvP safety
help: What the server does when it catches someone breaking the PvP safety rules: ban, kick, log, or nothing (Disabled). Log still stops the action, it just doesn't ban or kick anyone.

label: Anti-cheat: speed
help: What the server does when a player or vehicle moves faster than allowed: ban, kick, log, or nothing (Disabled). Log still stops the action, it just doesn't ban or kick anyone.

label: Anti-cheat: walking through walls
help: What the server does when a player walks through walls: ban, kick, log, or nothing (Disabled). Log still undoes the move and sends the player back, so anything that teleports players, like an RV interior mod, needs this Disabled. This is Disabled by default.

label: Anti-cheat: impossible hits
help: What the server does about impossible hits (damage, distance, weapon and vehicle hits): ban, kick, log, or nothing (Disabled). Log still stops the action, it just doesn't ban or kick anyone.

label: Anti-cheat: bad network messages
help: What the server does about broken or unexpected network messages: ban, kick, log only, or nothing (Disabled). This is Disabled by default.

label: Anti-cheat: role powers
help: What the server does when someone uses powers their role doesn't have: ban, kick, log, or nothing (Disabled). Log still stops the action, it just doesn't ban or kick anyone.

label: Anti-cheat: skill XP
help: What the server does about impossible skill XP gains: ban, kick, log only, or nothing (Disabled). The allowed amount follows the XP multiplier settings.

label: Anti-cheat: safehouse actions
help: What the server does about invalid safehouse actions (by owners, members or non-members): ban, kick, log, or nothing (Disabled). Log still stops the action, it just doesn't ban or kick anyone.

label: Anti-cheat: player data
help: What the server does about invalid player data or targets: ban, kick, log, or nothing (Disabled). Log still stops the action, it just doesn't ban or kick anyone.

label: Anti-cheat: file check
help: What the server does when a player's game files still don't match the server's 60 seconds after the file check: ban, kick, log only, or nothing (Disabled). It only applies while the file check setting is on.

label: Hide other players in list
help: On: the player list hides other players from each player.

label: Hide staff in player list
help: On: staff whose role allows hiding are left out of the player list.

label: Command log filter
help: Which client commands are left out of (minus) or kept in (plus) the cmd.txt log. Write rules like -vehicle.* and +vehicle.fixPart, separated by semicolons.

label: Logged player actions
help: Which player actions are written to the client action log, as action names separated by semicolons.

label: Log skill level changes
help: On: skill level changes are written to the PerkLog log.

label: Car speed limit (km/h)
help: The top speed for cars in multiplayer, in km/h. The speed anti-cheat uses the same number for vehicles.

label: Block car towing
help: On: players can't tow cars with cars in multiplayer.

label: Block trailer towing
help: On: players can't tow trailers in multiplayer.

label: Block towing burnt wrecks
help: On: players can't tow burnt-out wrecks in multiplayer.

label: Cars spawn
help: Off: no cars spawn in newly explored areas.

label: Car spawn rate
help: How many cars spawn in newly explored areas.

label: Engine loudness to zombies
help: Multiplies how loud every vehicle engine is to zombies. 1 is normal and 0 is quietest. Vehicles pick up a change when they next load or have a part changed, and 'Car noise range for zombies' multiplies on top of this on a server.

label: Easy car use
help: On: cars are unlocked and don't need keys to start. Newly found cars also come with a full tank, a full battery, a top quality engine and a key in the glove box, and engines never fail to start in the cold.

label: Fuel in found cars
help: How full the tanks of found cars are, for cars that have any fuel at all. In 42.21 Full gives the same amounts as Normal.

label: Locked cars
help: How often found cars are locked.

label: Fuel use
help: Multiplies how fast cars burn fuel.

label: Found car condition
help: The general state of found cars' parts.

label: Car crash damage
help: How much damage cars take in crashes.

label: Damage from being hit by a car
help: How much damage a player takes when hit by a car. When another player is driving, the PvP settings also decide whether the hit hurts.

label: Wrecked car traffic jams
help: On: traffic jams of wrecked cars appear in the places the map marks for them.

label: Car alarms
help: How often found cars have a working alarm.

label: Crashes hurt people inside
help: On: people inside a car can be hurt when it crashes.

label: Siren shutoff (hours)
help: In-game hours before a wailing car siren switches itself off. 0 means it doesn't switch off on its own.

label: Chance found cars have fuel
help: The chance a found car has any fuel at all.

label: Survivor cars
help: How often you find well kept cars that a survivor looked after.

label: Sirens attract zombies
help: On: zombies head towards car sirens.

label: Zombie count
help: The overall zombie amount. In the game's own settings screens, picking this also sets 'Population multiplier', but here they're separate boxes, so set both. The game also uses this directly for how many zombies are inside buildings and how dense the map is. None turns zombies off. Normal is the usual choice.

label: Zombie distribution
help: Urban Focused uses the map's own zombie density for each area, so density varies from place to place. Uniform gives every area the same density.

label: Zombie group randomness
help: On: random patches across the whole map have their zombie density set to zero as the map loads, so zombies are spread less evenly. Off: the map's own zombie density is used everywhere.

label: Zombie respawn
help: A shortcut in the game's own settings screens: picking this fills in 'Zombie respawn (hours)', 'Unseen time before respawn' and 'Zombie respawn share'. Here, set those three directly. None or Low is a common pick.

label: Zombie migration
help: A shortcut in the game's own settings screens: ticking this sets 'Zombie migration (hours)' to 12, and unticking sets 0. Here, set 'Zombie migration (hours)' directly.

label: Population multiplier
help: The actual size of the zombie population the game uses. The game's settings screens use these values: Insane 2.5, Very High 1.6, High 1.2, Normal 0.65, Low 0.15, None 0.

label: Starting zombie population
help: Multiplies the zombie population on day one. After that it grows towards the peak (see 'Peak multiplier' and 'Peak day').

label: Peak multiplier
help: Multiplies the zombie population on its peak day.

label: Peak day
help: The in-game day the zombie population reaches its peak.

label: Zombie respawn (hours)
help: How many in-game hours between zombie respawns into cleared areas. 0 means zombies don't respawn.

label: Unseen time before respawn
help: How many in-game hours an area has to go unseen by players before zombies can respawn there.

label: Zombie respawn share
help: What share of an area's population comes back each respawn, from 0 to 1.

label: Zombie migration (hours)
help: In-game hours between zombies drifting into empty areas, as the game describes it. The game says 0 stops migration.

label: Zombie sound follow distance
help: How far zombies try to walk towards the last sound they heard, as the game describes it.

label: Zombie group size
help: How many zombies like to gather into one wandering group. 0 or 1 turns grouping off.

label: Zombie group size variation
help: How much group size varies, as a percentage.

label: Distance to join a group
help: How far, in tiles, zombies walk to join a group.

label: Space between zombie groups
help: How far apart, in tiles, separate zombie groups stay.

label: Zombie group spread
help: How close, in tiles, group members stay to their group's leader.

label: Zombie crowd limit
help: How many zombies the server keeps in sync with each player before it starts deleting the extras to save performance. Only zombies that are outdoors, not chasing anyone and well away from that player are deleted. 0 means none are deleted.

label: Zombie speed
help: How fast zombies move. Random mixes speeds using 'Zombie sprinter percentage'. A zombie's speed is picked each time it's loaded into the world, and choosing Sprinters also makes zombies that are already loaded run. Casual groups often pick Shamblers or Fast Shamblers; players report sprinters can desync in multiplayer.

label: Sprinter percentage
help: When 'Zombie speed' is on Random, the percentage of zombies that sprint. The rest are shamblers or fast shamblers. Ignored for the other 'Zombie speed' choices.

label: Zombie strength
help: How hard zombies hit doors, windows, barricades and cars. It also sets how many zombies it takes to drag a character down (2 on Superhuman, 6 on Weak, 3 otherwise) and how easily a character fends off an attack. The damage a zombie's attack does to a character stays the same.

label: Zombie toughness
help: How hard zombies are to kill.

label: Infection spread
help: How the infection spreads. Blood and Saliva: bites always infect, and scratches and lacerations can too. Saliva Only: only bites infect. Everyone's Infected: wounds infect as usual, and everyone who dies comes back as a zombie, whatever killed them. None: wounds don't infect and nobody comes back.

label: Infection death time
help: How long an infected character has before the infection kills them. Never means the infection doesn't kill.

label: Reanimation time
help: How long after death an infected body gets back up as a zombie.

label: Zombie cognition
help: How smart zombies are, meaning whether they can open doors and windows. Random uses 'Zombie door opening percentage'.

label: Door opening percentage
help: When 'Zombie cognition' is on Random, the percentage of zombies that can open doors. Ignored for the other 'Zombie cognition' choices.

label: Zombies crawl under cars
help: How often zombies crawl under parked cars to reach you.

label: Zombie memory
help: How long zombies keep chasing after they lose sight or sound of you.

label: Zombie sight
help: How far zombies can see.

label: Zombie hearing
help: How far zombies can hear.

label: New stealth system
help: On: zombies use the newer sight rules, where a car between a zombie and a player on foot blocks its view and some objects give cover to sneaking players. Off: the older rules, which weigh light, distance and movement differently. Traits, rain and fog count either way.

label: Idle zombies bash things
help: On: wandering zombies that haven't noticed anyone can still bash doors and builds.

label: Zombies damage builds
help: On: zombies can damage and destroy things players have built.

label: Zombie active time
help: When zombies are fully active: Both, Night or Day. Outside their active time they move as shamblers whatever 'Zombie speed' says, are a quarter as likely to spot players, and forget them quickly.

label: Zombies set off alarms
help: On: zombies breaking windows can set off house alarms.

label: Zombie drag down
help: On: a group of zombies attacking at once can drag a character down and kill them.

label: Crawlers help drag down
help: On: crawlers next to you also count towards being dragged down.

label: Zombie lunge
help: On: zombies can lunge at you right after climbing a fence or window if you're standing too close.

label: Zombie armour strength
help: Multiplies how much protection zombies get from armour they're wearing.

label: Zombie armour cap (%)
help: The most protection, as a percentage, worn armour can give a zombie.

label: Zombies with stuck weapons (%)
help: Percentage chance a zombie has a weapon stuck in it.

label: Zombie fall damage
help: Multiplies the damage zombies take from falling.

label: Fake dead zombies
help: Whether some bodies that look dead get up and attack: world zombies only, world and combat zombies, or never.

label: Clear zombies at spawn
help: Clears zombies from where a new character spawns: the building and around it, the building, the room, or nowhere.

label: Zombies to damage fences
help: How many zombies it takes to start damaging a tall fence. Once a fence starts bending, fewer are needed. Below 1, zombies don't bend tall fences.

label: Fence damage speed
help: How quickly zombies damage tall fences.

label: No loot respawn in safehouses
help: On: loot doesn't respawn inside claimed safehouses. Only matters when 'Loot respawn (hours)' is above 0.

label: Perishable food loot
help: Loot amount for food that can rot in containers. 0 means none. The settings screen choices are 0.05 insanely rare, 0.2 extremely rare, 0.4 rare, 0.6 normal, 2 common and 3 abundant.

label: Other reading loot
help: Loot amount for books, fliers and newspapers (not skill books) in containers. 0 means none. The settings screen choices are 0.05 insanely rare, 0.2 extremely rare, 0.4 rare, 0.6 normal, 2 common and 3 abundant.

label: Skill book loot
help: Loot amount for skill books in containers. 0 means none. The settings screen choices are 0.05 insanely rare, 0.2 extremely rare, 0.4 rare, 0.6 normal, 2 common and 3 abundant.

label: Recipe item loot
help: Loot amount for items that teach recipes in containers. 0 means none. The settings screen choices are 0.05 insanely rare, 0.2 extremely rare, 0.4 rare, 0.6 normal, 2 common and 3 abundant.

label: Medical loot
help: Loot amount for medicine, bandages and first aid tools in containers. 0 means none. The settings screen choices are 0.05 insanely rare, 0.2 extremely rare, 0.4 rare, 0.6 normal, 2 common and 3 abundant.

label: Survival gear loot
help: Loot amount for camping and fishing gear in containers. 0 means none. The settings screen choices are 0.05 insanely rare, 0.2 extremely rare, 0.4 rare, 0.6 normal, 2 common and 3 abundant.

label: Non-perishable food loot
help: Loot amount for canned and dried food and drinks in containers. 0 means none. The settings screen choices are 0.05 insanely rare, 0.2 extremely rare, 0.4 rare, 0.6 normal, 2 common and 3 abundant.

label: Melee weapon loot
help: Loot amount for melee weapons in containers. 0 means none. The settings screen choices are 0.05 insanely rare, 0.2 extremely rare, 0.4 rare, 0.6 normal, 2 common and 3 abundant.

label: Ranged weapon loot
help: Loot amount for guns and attachments in containers. 0 means none. The settings screen choices are 0.05 insanely rare, 0.2 extremely rare, 0.4 rare, 0.6 normal, 2 common and 3 abundant.

label: Ammo loot
help: Loot amount for ammo, boxes and magazines in containers. 0 means none. The settings screen choices are 0.05 insanely rare, 0.2 extremely rare, 0.4 rare, 0.6 normal, 2 common and 3 abundant.

label: Mechanics loot
help: Loot amount for car parts and their tools in containers. 0 means none. The settings screen choices are 0.05 insanely rare, 0.2 extremely rare, 0.4 rare, 0.6 normal, 2 common and 3 abundant.

label: Other loot
help: How often items that don't fit any other loot category spawn in containers. None stops them spawning. Foraging in towns and along roads isn't tied to this: it follows Nature's Abundance.

label: Clothing loot
help: Loot amount for clothing in containers. 0 means none. The settings screen choices are 0.05 insanely rare, 0.2 extremely rare, 0.4 rare, 0.6 normal, 2 common and 3 abundant.

label: Bag loot
help: Loot amount for bags and cases in containers. 0 means none. The settings screen choices are 0.05 insanely rare, 0.2 extremely rare, 0.4 rare, 0.6 normal, 2 common and 3 abundant.

label: Key loot
help: Loot amount for keys, key rings and locks in containers. 0 means none. The settings screen choices are 0.05 insanely rare, 0.2 extremely rare, 0.4 rare, 0.6 normal, 2 common and 3 abundant. This also sets the chance zombies and cars carry keys.

label: Media loot
help: Loot amount for VHS tapes and CDs in containers. 0 means none. The settings screen choices are 0.05 insanely rare, 0.2 extremely rare, 0.4 rare, 0.6 normal, 2 common and 3 abundant.

label: Memento loot
help: Loot amount for Spiffo items, plushies and keepsakes in containers. 0 means none. The settings screen choices are 0.05 insanely rare, 0.2 extremely rare, 0.4 rare, 0.6 normal, 2 common and 3 abundant.

label: Cooking loot
help: Loot amount for cooking items in containers. 0 means none. The settings screen choices are 0.05 insanely rare, 0.2 extremely rare, 0.4 rare, 0.6 normal, 2 common and 3 abundant.

label: Material loot
help: Loot amount for crafting and building materials in containers. 0 means none. The settings screen choices are 0.05 insanely rare, 0.2 extremely rare, 0.4 rare, 0.6 normal, 2 common and 3 abundant.

label: Farming loot
help: Loot amount for seeds and farming tools in containers. 0 means none. The settings screen choices are 0.05 insanely rare, 0.2 extremely rare, 0.4 rare, 0.6 normal, 2 common and 3 abundant.

label: Tool loot
help: Loot amount for other tools in containers. 0 means none. The settings screen choices are 0.05 insanely rare, 0.2 extremely rare, 0.4 rare, 0.6 normal, 2 common and 3 abundant.

label: Loot rolls multiplier
help: Multiplies how many times each container's loot table is rolled. The game warns not to change this; high values can hurt performance.

label: Items that never spawn
help: Item types, separated by commas, that never spawn as normal loot. Spaces are ignored. Foraging uses this list too.

label: Keep removed items out of stories
help: On: items on the loot removal list, or in a loot category set to None, also stay out of the random story scenes placed around the world. Off: those scenes can still place them.

label: Keep removed items off zombies
help: On: weapons the game attaches to zombies skip any item on the loot removal list or in a loot category set to None. Clothing zombies wear isn't affected.

label: More loot near zombies
help: Above 0, places with more zombies nearby get more loot, scaled by this number. 0 turns this off.

label: Insanely rare loot factor
help: The spawn multiplier for generators when 'Generators' is set to Insanely Rare. Nothing else in Build 42.21 reads this.

label: Extremely rare loot factor
help: The spawn multiplier for generators when 'Generators' is set to Extremely Rare. Nothing else in Build 42.21 reads this.

label: Rare loot factor
help: The spawn multiplier for generators when 'Generators' is set to Rare. Nothing else in Build 42.21 reads this.

label: Normal loot factor
help: The spawn multiplier for generators when 'Generators' is set to Normal. Nothing else in Build 42.21 reads this.

label: Common loot factor
help: The spawn multiplier for generators when 'Generators' is set to Common. Nothing else in Build 42.21 reads this.

label: Abundant loot factor
help: The spawn multiplier for generators when 'Generators' is set to Abundant. Nothing else in Build 42.21 reads this.

label: No respawn where seen (hours)
help: Stops loot refilling in a town area if players have been there within this many in-game hours. 0 turns the check off, so areas refill on schedule even if players were just there. Only matters when 'Loot respawn (hours)' is above 0.

label: Loot respawn (hours)
help: How often looted containers in towns refill, in in-game hours. Only containers that have been looted at least once refill, and 0 turns it off. It's off in every Build 42 preset; servers that use it often pick 168 to 720 hours (1 week to 1 month).

label: Full container limit
help: Containers holding this many items or more don't refill.

label: No loot respawn in built areas
help: On: once players build, barricade, hang sheets or place furniture somewhere, loot stops respawning across that whole map zone, not just in that building.

label: Ground items to clear
help: Item types, separated by commas, that are cleared from the ground once 'Ground item removal (hours)' have passed since they were dropped. They're cleared when that part of the map next loads.

label: Ground item removal (hours)
help: How many in-game hours an item has to lie on the ground before the removal list clears it. It goes the next time that part of the map loads.

label: Reverse the ground clear list
help: Off: items on the world item removal list are cleared from the ground once they've lain there long enough. On: the list becomes a keep list, and ground items that aren't on it are cleared instead.

label: Generators
help: How often generators turn up, from none to abundant. This covers generators in containers and generators placed in sheds, garages and storage rooms the first time they're seen; in rural ones it also sets the chance of a random workstation. For container loot, this is the only setting that uses the six Loot Factor settings.

label: Annotated maps
help: How often a found map has a dead survivor's notes on it.

label: Corpse removal (hours)
help: How many in-game hours before dead bodies rot away and disappear. 0 or -1 means bodies stay and don't grow maggots. Player bodies follow the server setting 'Remove player bodies too'.

label: Rotten food removal (days)
help: How many in-game days after food rots before it's removed from the map. -1 means never.

label: Largest building that can be pre-looted
help: Buildings with more rooms than this aren't pre-looted or trashed. Shops are the exception: they can still turn up already looted whatever their size.

label: Blood splat lifespan (days)
help: Days before old blood splats are cleaned away, checked when that part of the map loads. 0 means they stay forever. This is the copy the game reads, not the server setting of the same name.

label: Highest pre-looted building chance
help: The highest chance, in percent, that a building is already looted and trashed when it's first found.

label: Days to highest pre-looted chance
help: How many days it takes to reach the 'Highest pre-looted building chance'. Before that, the chance grows day by day.

label: Rural pre-looted chance multiplier
help: Meant to multiply the already-looted chance for buildings outside towns, but the game drops the decimals first. Below 1, rural buildings get the lowest chance (1 percent) and lose no loot over time; from 1 to just under 2 nothing changes; 2 doubles both.

label: Most loot lost over time (%)
help: The highest share of loot, in percent, that stops spawning as days pass.

label: Days to most loot lost
help: How many days it takes to reach the 'Most loot lost over time (%)' amount.

label: Day length
help: How long one in-game day lasts in real time. 2 hour days are a common choice for Build 42.

label: Start year
help: The year the world starts in, from 1993 up to 2092. Not shown in the game's settings screens.

label: Start month
help: The month the world starts in.

label: Start day of the month
help: The day of the month the world starts on.

label: Start hour
help: The hour of the day the world starts at.

label: Day and night cycle
help: Normal days and nights, endless day, or endless night.

label: Nature regrowth speed
help: How many days until nature fully takes over (grass, vines and trees). This is fixed when the world is created, because the world keeps its own erosion file.

label: Nature regrowth days
help: A custom number of days for nature to fully take over. 0 uses 'Nature regrowth speed'. -1 stops nature growing at all, and that works on a running world too.

label: Months since the outbreak
help: How many months after the outbreak the world begins, from 0 to 12. This sets how overgrown the world is when it's created, and affects bodies and skeletons in areas when they're first loaded. It also counts towards 'Water shutoff day' and 'Power shutoff day', so at 1 month or more, a 14 day shutoff means water and power are already off when the world starts. It doesn't change the start date.

label: Night darkness
help: How dark nights are, from pitch black to bright.

label: Length of nights
help: How long nights are, from always night to always day. Not shown in the game's settings screens.

label: Weather pattern
help: Normal weather, or weather locked to one state: no weather, endless rain, endless storm, endless snow or endless blizzard.

label: Fog pattern
help: Normal fog, no fog, or endless fog.

label: Temperature
help: Shifts how cold or hot the seasons are. Applied each time the world loads.

label: Rain
help: How often it rains.

label: Foraging finds
help: How many items players find when foraging.

label: Thickest fog on screen
help: Caps how thick fog can look on screen.

label: Heaviest rain on screen
help: Caps how heavy rain looks on screen.

label: Snow on the ground
help: On: snow builds up on the ground. Off: snow still shows on plants and roofs.

label: Vermin level
help: How common and heavy rat and other vermin infestations are. 0 means none.

label: Days to full vermin level
help: How many days it takes for vermin to reach the 'Vermin level' you've set.

label: Fish numbers
help: How many fish are in rivers and lakes.

label: Clay by lakes chance
help: The chance that dirt by lakes is turned into clay when the world generates new ground.

label: Clay by rivers chance
help: The chance that dirt by rivers is turned into clay when the world generates new ground.

label: Water shutoff range (single player)
help: A range for when tap water stops. Only the single player new game screen uses this, to roll a random day into 'Water shutoff day'. Servers read 'Water shutoff day' directly, and the Host screen hides this choice.

label: Power shutoff range (single player)
help: A range for when the power grid shuts off. Only the single player new game screen uses this, to roll a random day into 'Power shutoff day'. Servers read 'Power shutoff day' directly, and the Host screen hides this choice.

label: Alarm battery life
help: How long house alarm batteries last after the power goes. Rolled for each alarmed building when the map's building data is set up. Only used when a new world is created, and for buildings from maps added to it later: saved buildings keep what they rolled.

label: Water shutoff day
help: The day tap water stops, counted from the outbreak, so 'Months since the outbreak' counts towards it. -1 turns the water off from the very start. For water that never stops in practice, use a very large number such as 100000. Utilities going off around 30 days is common.

label: Power shutoff day
help: The day the power grid shuts off, counted from the outbreak, so 'Months since the outbreak' counts towards it. -1 means there's no grid power from the very start. For power that never shuts off in practice, use a very large number such as 100000. Utilities going off around 30 days is common.

label: Alarm battery decay number
help: 'Alarm battery life' is the one the game uses. Not shown in the game's settings screens.

label: Generator fuel use
help: Multiplies how much fuel a generator burns each in-game hour. A generator burns more the more it's powering, and 0 means it burns no fuel.

label: Generators work outdoors
help: On: generators work outdoors, which lets them power things such as fuel pumps.

label: Endless fuel pumps
help: On: fuel pumps never run dry. This overrides the pump minimum, maximum and empty chance settings.

label: Fuel pump lowest starting fill
help: The lowest amount of fuel a pump starts with, from 0 (empty) to 1 (full).

label: Fuel pump highest starting fill
help: The highest amount of fuel a pump starts with, from 0 (empty) to 1 (full).

label: Fuel pump empty chance
help: The chance, in percent, that a fuel pump starts empty.

label: Light bulb lifespan
help: How long light bulbs last. Higher lasts longer, and 0 means bulbs never break. Car headlights aren't affected.

label: Generator range (tiles)
help: How far, in tiles, a generator sends power sideways.

label: Generator range (floors)
help: How many floors above and below a generator get power.

label: Farming speed (old)
help: The old farming speed choice, hidden from the game's settings screens. 'Farming speed', the number box, is the one used.

label: Compost time
help: How long food takes to turn into compost, from 1 to 12 weeks.

label: Food spoilage speed
help: How fast food spoils, in or out of a fridge.

label: Fridge effectiveness
help: How well fridges keep food fresh. No decay means chilled food never spoils.

label: Crop toughness
help: How much water crops lose each day and how well they resist disease.

label: Harvest size (old)
help: The old harvest size choice, hidden from the game's settings screens. Its replacement, 'Harvest size', doesn't change harvests in 42.21 either.

label: Animal hunger and thirst
help: How fast animals get hungry and thirsty.

label: Animal hunger when unwatched
help: How fast animals get hungry and thirsty while nobody's nearby. Not shown in the game's settings screens.

label: Animal pregnancy time
help: How long animal pregnancies last.

label: Animal ageing speed
help: How fast animals age. Slow and Very Slow work the same as Normal.

label: Milk build-up speed
help: How fast animals build up milk.

label: Wool growth speed
help: How fast animals grow wool.

label: Farms start with animals
help: How often farms start with animals.

label: Grass regrowth (hours)
help: In-game hours for grass to grow back after animals eat it or it's cut.

label: Unseen fox takes chickens
help: On: an unseen predator may kill chickens or turkeys in a hutch if its door is left open at night.

label: Breeding season
help: On: animals only breed and lay in their season. Off: all year.

label: Egg hatch time
help: How long eggs take to hatch.

label: Animal noise draws zombies
help: On: animal noises draw nearby zombies.

label: Animal tracks
help: How often wild animals leave tracks.

label: Animal paths
help: How often animal paths for hunting are created when the world generates new areas.

label: Players can poison food
help: Whether players can add poison to food: True for yes, False for no, or yes except bleach.

label: Maggots on corpses
help: Where maggots can appear on corpses: in and around bodies, in bodies only, or never.

label: Indoor crops die
help: On: crops and herbs grown indoors slowly lose health until they die. House plants, and crops in a greenhouse, aren't affected.

label: Growing seasons
help: On: seasons matter for crops. Players can sow any month, but crops sown outside their season start weaker, outdoor crops suffer in their bad months and in winter unless they're cold hardy, and sowing in a crop's best month can give a bonus harvest. Off: crops grow the same all year.

label: Farming above ground floor
help: On: players can farm above the ground floor. The game warns this can hurt performance.

label: Farming speed
help: Multiplies how fast crops grow.

label: Harvest size
help: Meant to multiply how much a crop gives at harvest. In 42.21 the game works out the multiplied amount but then hands out the normal one, so this doesn't change harvests.

label: Most fuel in a fire (hours)
help: The most hours of fuel a campfire or stove can hold.

label: Hunger, thirst and tiredness speed
help: How fast hunger, thirst and tiredness build up.

label: Starter kit
help: On: new characters start with chips, a water bottle, a small backpack, a baseball bat and a hammer.

label: Nutrition
help: On: what characters eat affects their weight and health.

label: Endurance recovery
help: How fast characters get their breath back after effort.

label: Extra trait points
help: Extra trait points at character creation. A negative number gives fewer.

label: All clothing unlocked
help: On: every clothing item can be picked at character creation.

label: Unseen media in media list
help: How the media list shows media your players haven't seen yet: fully revealed, shown as ???, or completely hidden.

label: See unlearnt recipes
help: On: players can see recipes at a crafting station before they've learnt them.

label: Media XP level cap
help: From this skill level up, TV, VHS and other media stop giving XP for that skill.

label: Scrapping XP level cap
help: From this skill level up, scrapping furniture stops giving XP for that skill, so 0 means scrapping gives no XP. Electrical isn't affected and always gives XP.

label: Re-reading cooldown (days)
help: How many in-game days before re-reading the same magazine or book helps again.

label: Negative traits penalty
help: Whether picking many negative traits gives fewer bonus points. None means no penalty.

label: Minutes per skill book page
help: How many in-game minutes it takes to read one page of a skill book.

label: Muscle strain
help: Multiplies muscle strain from swinging weapons and tools, firing guns and carrying heavy loads. 0 turns that strain off, but some crafting actions still cause strain whatever this is set to.

label: Clothing discomfort
help: Multiplies discomfort from worn clothing. 0 turns clothing discomfort off. Worn bags aren't affected by this.

label: No black clothes
help: On: randomly tinted clothes skip the darkest, near black shades.

label: Easy climbing
help: On: climbing sheet ropes and walls never fails.

label: Global
help: Multiplies XP for every skill, but only while the global multiplier is switched on. 1.5 to 2 is common; public listings advertise 2 to 3.

label: Use the global multiplier
help: On: the global XP multiplier applies to every skill and the per-skill multipliers are ignored. Off: each skill uses its own multiplier.

label: Fitness
help: Multiplies XP for the Fitness skill. Only used when the global multiplier is switched off.

label: Strength
help: Multiplies XP for the Strength skill. Only used when the global multiplier is switched off.

label: Sprinting
help: Multiplies XP for the Sprinting skill. Only used when the global multiplier is switched off.

label: Lightfooted
help: Multiplies XP for the Lightfooted skill. Only used when the global multiplier is switched off.

label: Nimble
help: Multiplies XP for the Nimble skill. Only used when the global multiplier is switched off.

label: Sneaking
help: Multiplies XP for the Sneaking skill. Only used when the global multiplier is switched off.

label: Axe
help: Multiplies XP for the Axe skill. Only used when the global multiplier is switched off.

label: Long blunt
help: Multiplies XP for the Long Blunt skill. Only used when the global multiplier is switched off.

label: Short blunt
help: Multiplies XP for the Short Blunt skill. Only used when the global multiplier is switched off.

label: Long blade
help: Multiplies XP for the Long Blade skill. Only used when the global multiplier is switched off.

label: Short blade
help: Multiplies XP for the Short Blade skill. Only used when the global multiplier is switched off.

label: Spear
help: Multiplies XP for the Spear skill. Only used when the global multiplier is switched off.

label: Maintenance
help: Multiplies XP for the Maintenance skill. Only used when the global multiplier is switched off.

label: Carpentry
help: Multiplies XP for the Carpentry skill. Only used when the global multiplier is switched off.

label: Cooking
help: Multiplies XP for the Cooking skill. Only used when the global multiplier is switched off.

label: Agriculture
help: Multiplies XP for the Agriculture skill. Only used when the global multiplier is switched off.

label: First aid
help: Multiplies XP for the First Aid skill. Only used when the global multiplier is switched off.

label: Electrical
help: Multiplies XP for the Electrical skill. Only used when the global multiplier is switched off.

label: Welding
help: Multiplies XP for the Welding skill. Only used when the global multiplier is switched off.

label: Mechanics
help: Multiplies XP for the Mechanics skill. Only used when the global multiplier is switched off.

label: Tailoring
help: Multiplies XP for the Tailoring skill. Only used when the global multiplier is switched off.

label: Aiming
help: Multiplies XP for the Aiming skill. Only used when the global multiplier is switched off.

label: Reloading
help: Multiplies XP for the Reloading skill. Only used when the global multiplier is switched off.

label: Fishing
help: Multiplies XP for the Fishing skill. Only used when the global multiplier is switched off.

label: Trapping
help: Multiplies XP for the Trapping skill. Only used when the global multiplier is switched off.

label: Foraging
help: Multiplies XP for the Foraging skill. Only used when the global multiplier is switched off.

label: Knapping
help: Multiplies XP for the Knapping skill. Only used when the global multiplier is switched off.

label: Masonry
help: Multiplies XP for the Masonry skill. Only used when the global multiplier is switched off.

label: Pottery
help: Multiplies XP for the Pottery skill. Only used when the global multiplier is switched off.

label: Carving
help: Multiplies XP for the Carving skill. Only used when the global multiplier is switched off.

label: Animal care
help: Multiplies XP for the Animal Care skill. Only used when the global multiplier is switched off.

label: Tracking
help: Multiplies XP for the Tracking skill. Only used when the global multiplier is switched off.

label: Blacksmithing
help: Multiplies XP for the Blacksmithing skill. Only used when the global multiplier is switched off.

label: Butchering
help: Multiplies XP for the Butchering skill. Only used when the global multiplier is switched off.

label: Glassmaking
help: Multiplies XP for the Glassmaking skill. Only used when the global multiplier is switched off.

label: Player-built construction strength
help: How many bonus hit points player-built things get on top of their base hit points, so they last longer against zombies. Normal gives the usual bonus, Very Low halves it and Very High adds half again. It's set when each thing is built.

label: Broken bones
help: On: characters can break bones from falls, being hit by a car and car crashes.

label: Injury severity
help: How bad injuries are and how long they take to heal.

label: Rotting bodies affect health
help: How much rotting bodies nearby make a character sick. Sickness only starts with more than 5 bodies nearby. None turns this off.

label: Zombies affect health
help: On: living zombies nearby count like rotting bodies, so they can make a character sick too. This does nothing when 'Rotting bodies affect health' is None.

label: Blood amount
help: How much blood sprays onto floors and walls, from None to Ultra Gore.

label: Clothing wear
help: How much blood and dirt clothes pick up, and how dirty, bloody and torn zombies' clothes are when they spawn. This doesn't change how fast clothes lose condition. In 42.21, Fast adds less blood and dirt to clothes than Normal does.

label: Fire spreads
help: On: fire spreads to nearby things.

label: Melee swings slow you
help: On: some attack and body dragging animations slow you down while they play.

label: Tainted water tooltip
help: On: tainted water and tainted food are labelled as tainted, and automatic drinking skips tainted water. Off: tainted water isn't labelled, and automatic drinking can pick it.

label: Hit several zombies per swing
help: On: some melee weapons can hit several zombies in one swing.

label: Bites from behind
help: How likely a zombie attacking from behind or the side is to injure or bite. High is the most dangerous.

label: Infected wound damage
help: Lets infected wounds hurt a character who's already at the worst level of sickness. 0 turns this damage off, and higher values make it kick in sooner.

label: Gun damage chance
help: What happens when a gunshot fails its hit roll. Disabled: it misses. Zombies only: a zombie is still hit but takes no damage, and other targets are missed. All types of target: any target is still hit but takes no damage.

label: Gunshot noise range
help: Multiplies how far away zombies can hear gunshots.

label: Gun jam chance
help: Multiplies the chance guns jam. 0 means guns never jam.

label: Moodles affect aim
help: Multiplies how much moodles (panic, tiredness and so on) hurt aim. 0 turns that off.

label: Weather affects aim
help: Multiplies how much wind, rain and fog hurt aim. 0 turns that off.

label: Headgear affects aim
help: On: headgear such as welding masks affects aim.

label: Mini-map allowed
help: On: players can open a mini-map. This only works when 'World map allowed' is on.

label: World map allowed
help: On: players can open the full world map.

label: Whole map revealed at start
help: On: the world map starts fully revealed.

label: Maps need light to read
help: On: players can't open the world map when it's too dark to read, unless they're holding or wearing a light or sitting in a car with a working battery. Admins aren't affected. Paper maps need light whatever this is set to.

label: House alarms
help: How likely a house is to have an alarm. This is rolled for buildings when the map's building data is set up. Only used when a new world is created, and for buildings from maps added to it later: saved buildings keep what they rolled.

label: Locked houses
help: How often house doors and windows are locked. Each door or window is set when it's first created from the map.

label: Helicopter event
help: How often the helicopter event flies over. The first flyover is picked for 6 to 9 nights in when the world starts and saved with the world, so switching to Never later doesn't cancel it. After that, Sometimes repeats every 10 to 15 days and Often every 6 to 9.

label: Distant noise events
help: How often far-off events like gunshots happen, drawing zombies.

label: Events while sleeping
help: Meant to control zombie break-ins while a character sleeps, but in 42.21 the game never switches the break-in check on, so this has no effect. Nightmares happen whatever this is set to.

label: Building stories
help: How often buildings get a story set-up, such as burnt out, a stash or bodies. This is rolled the first time a building is loaded.

label: Road stories
help: How often road stories appear, such as police roadblocks.

label: Zone stories
help: How often scene stories appear in map zones, such as a forest campsite.

label: Basements
help: Shown in the game's settings screens as how often basements appear.
